# vibe's ENTIRE transitive tree, hash-pinned (Dockerfile step 6b, C9).
#
# `uv pip install --require-hashes -r` against this file is the PyPI twin of
# `npm ci` against package-lock.json: the version is named, and so is every byte
# behind it. `mistral-vibe` pulls 96 transitive packages, and a bare
# `pip install mistral-vibe==3.1.4` re-resolves every one of them per build and
# accepts whatever wheel PyPI serves for each today.
#
# THE INTERPRETER IS NOT THE BASE IMAGE'S, and that is why the resolution flags
# below differ from aider's. `mistral-vibe` declares `requires_python >=3.12`;
# bookworm-slim ships 3.11.2. The Dockerfile installs a pinned, checksummed
# CPython 3.12 standalone under /opt/mllm/real/python3.12 (cli-versions.lock:
# artifacts.python312) and builds this venv against it, because
# `UV_PYTHON_DOWNLOADS=never` forbids uv fetching one -- and an unpinned remote
# interpreter would breach §7.3's first unconditional constraint anyway.
#
# REGENERATE (from the repo root, when the pinned vibe version moves):
#
#     echo 'mistral-vibe==<version>' > /tmp/vibe.in
#     uv pip compile --generate-hashes --no-header --no-annotate \
#         --python-version 3.12 --python-platform x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu \
#         -o skills/multi-llm/tests/container/vibe-requirements.txt /tmp/vibe.in
#
# The two resolution flags are not optional: they must match the venv's
# interpreter and the image platform (cli-versions.lock: artifacts.python312,
# platform), or the markers resolve for the developer's machine and the build
# fails on a wheel that does not exist there.
